prompt:
Create one finished flat opaque landscape 16:9 cultural-event poster for subway and community digital displays. Adult neighbours should recognize both an outdoor short-film screening and a director speaking with the audience. Use a bold architectural graphic system: the poster itself forms a frontal bridge section, its two piers and upper span sheltering a substantial illustrated cinema scene. Crisp drawn edges, mineral blue structure, warm white lettering and information territories, restrained coral clothes and mats. Civic, inviting, contemporary; carefully drawn adults, no childish toy styling or photorealistic mockup.

Composition measured on a 720-wide viewing version (scale all type and spacing proportionally at native output):
• Broad left title pier occupies x4–35%, y12–86%. The Korean headline uses three original word groups on three lines, square strong Korean sans, 60–66px, controlled counters and consistent Hangul proportions. English is a separate 17–19px baseline beneath.
• Long upper-right schedule lintel x42–96%, y8–25%, a warm white rectangle tied into the blue bridge. Date and time are 25–30px, on two clear lines.
• Programme descriptor is a full flat horizontal baseline directly above the arch scene, x40–96%, y30–39%, at least 17px.
• Central open arch x38–74%, y42–95% is a substantial warm-white opening bounded by the blue bridge, with a shallow curved upper arch and vertical sides. It holds a frontal graphic event scene: freestanding projection screen on its left with a clearly visible nontext film still; several adults seated on distinctly drawn mats across the floor; a standing adult on the right visibly holding a microphone toward their mouth and gesturing to seated listeners. Adult body structure, distinct limbs, grounded mat contact and readable screen/microphone shapes. Show small glimpses of the stream-bank setting through the opening. The structure and actual screen/people/mats/microphone carry the event content, not letter-shaped objects or a tiny icon.
• Right practical pier x78–97%, y42–96%, warm-white territory with mineral-blue type, all 137px of available width at 720 used for readable lettering, no extra inset stealing width. Practical text is 17px with 21px leading and approximately 7px gaps between the five entry groups. Venue wraps after its second word, free-entry/capacity wraps after the middle dot, weather wraps before the final word; arrival and mat entries remain single lines. Keep word spaces intact across soft wraps. Eight practical lines fit the full-height pier.

Print exactly these ten entries once each, no heading labels or quote marks. Preserve spelling, lettercase, digits, word spaces, middle dots and the time en dash. The title may soft-wrap only between its original three word groups; other wrapping only at word boundaries as described:
Left headline: "다리 아래 영화관"
Left English baseline: "BRIDGE CINEMA"
Programme above the scene: "야외 단편 상영 · 감독과의 대화"
Schedule date: "2026.12.05 토요일"
Schedule time: "18:00–20:30"
Right column, first group: "홍제천 연가교 아래"
Right column, second group: "17:30부터 입장"
Right column, third group: "돗자리 지참"
Right column, fourth group: "무료 관람 · 선착순 80명"
Right column, fifth group: "우천 시 실내로 변경"

All required information must remain readable in the 720-wide use view. Keep the first gaze on the title pier and cinema arch, then the schedule span, descriptor and usable practical column. Clean local edges and flat high contrast; conventional printed lettering integrated with the architecture. No additional text anywhere, no logos, pseudo-print, watermark, QR, style labels, decorative glyphs, contact sheet, border mockup or extra poster.
